title: Payment Plan Agreement
summary: Let a customer or debtor pay an existing balance over time, with a schedule and what happens if a payment is missed.
useWhen: Someone owes you money, for example an unpaid invoice, rent arrears or damages, and you agree to accept installments.
watchOuts: In many states, a written acknowledgment of a debt or a partial payment can restart the statute of limitations. Debtors should know this. Creditors should not use it to revive time-barred debts in a misleading way.
Third-party debt collectors are subject to the federal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act and Regulation F, and to state collection laws.

If you agree to accept less than the full balance, say clearly whether the remainder is forgiven only on full performance. Forgiven debt can be taxable income to the debtor (Form 1099-C rules may apply).
Autopay authorizations for recurring debits must meet Regulation E and card-network rules.

variables.label: Creditor: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Debtor: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: What the balance is for
variables.help: Invoice numbers, services, rent period, etc.

variables.label: Is the creditor accepting less than the full balance?
variables.help: If on, the creditor accepts a reduced amount if every payment is made on time.

variables.label: Reduced settlement amount
variables.help: Amount accepted in full satisfaction if all payments are made on time.

variables.label: Days to cure a missed payment
variables.help: Grace period after written notice before the plan is in default.

variables.label: Interest during the plan
variables.default: no interest if paid on schedule
options: no interest if paid on schedule

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 1. Parties and balance
sections.body:
**Creditor:** {{creditor_name}}, {{creditor_address}} ({{creditor_email}})

**Debtor:** {{debtor_name}}, {{debtor_address}} ({{debtor_email}})

Debtor owes Creditor {{total_balance}} as of {{agreement_date}} for: {{debt_description}}. Debtor confirms this amount is correct.

sections.title: 2. Payment schedule
sections.body: Debtor will pay {{down_payment}} on signing, then {{number_of_payments}} installments of {{installment_amount}}, paid {{frequency}}, starting {{first_due}}, by {{payment_method}}. Debtor may pay more or pay off early at any time.

sections.title: 3. Interest
sections.body: During the plan: {{interest_on_plan}}. If interest applies, it is {{plan_rate}}% per year on the unpaid balance, never above the legal maximum.

sections.title: 4. Reduced settlement
sections.body: If Debtor makes every payment on time, Creditor will accept {{settlement_amount}} in full satisfaction of the balance and will confirm in writing that the account is settled. If Debtor defaults, this reduction does not apply and the full balance, minus payments made, is owed.

sections.title: 5. Missed payments
sections.body: If a payment is missed, Creditor will give Debtor written notice. If Debtor does not pay the missed amount within {{cure_days}} days after notice, the plan is in default and Creditor may demand the entire remaining balance and pursue any lawful remedy.

sections.title: 6. Creditor's promises
sections.body: While Debtor is not in default, Creditor will not start collection action or report the account as delinquent for the period covered by this plan, and will credit every payment promptly. Creditor will provide a payment history on request.

sections.title: 7. No other changes
sections.body: This agreement only changes the payment terms for the balance described. It does not waive any other rights.

sections.title: 8. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Creditor** — {{creditor_name}}

[[sig:creditor]]

Printed name: [[name:creditor]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:creditor:Title]]
Date: [[date:creditor]]

**Debtor** — {{debtor_name}}

[[sig:debtor]]

Printed name: [[name:debtor]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:debtor:Title]]
Date: [[date:debtor]]
